positions.summary_short: Morgan would accelerate office-to-residential and heritage conversions, and expand micro-modular shelters while pressing senior governments for homelessness funding.
summary_bullets: Would accelerate affordable, supportive, market-rate, office-to-residential, and heritage-to-residential housing conversions: 'Empty buildings should become homes, underutilized spaces should become community'
Cites 190 homes created from 180,000+ sq. ft. of underused office space, including deeply affordable housing
Would expand 'practical, dignified shelter options' including the micro-modular shelter program, while pushing the province and federal government for investments to address homelessness at its roots
positions.verbatim_quote: We will accelerate affordable, supportive, market-rate, office-to-residential, and heritage-to-residential housing conversions. Empty buildings should become homes, underutilized spaces should become community.
positions.source_title: Re-Elect Josh Morgan for Mayor (campaign platform)

positions.summary_short: Morgan would launch late-night transit service for shift workers, finish the BRT corridors under construction, and complete the Wharncliffe underpass.
summary_bullets: Would launch an 'Alternative Delivery Service' reaching more neighbourhoods and employment areas with better hours, for workers (industrial parks, hospitals, restaurants, entertainment, overnight operations) needing reliable service beyond 11 p.m.
Would finish and open the rapid transit corridors already underway (East London Link, Wellington Gateway), then plan the next phase of a connected citywide network
Would complete the Wharncliffe Road underpass and move quickly on improvements at Bostwick Road and Bradley Avenue: 'Infrastructure should lead growth, not chase it'
Would close gaps in the Thames Valley Parkway trail and strengthen regional transportation links, including rail service and more destinations from London International Airport
positions.verbatim_quote: We will finish and open the rapid transit corridors already underway, then continue planning for the next phase of a connected citywide network.
positions.source_title: Re-Elect Josh Morgan for Mayor (campaign platform)

positions.summary_short: Morgan would hold property tax increases in the 3% range over four years via disciplined budgeting and more senior-government funding.
summary_bullets: Would hold property tax increases 'in the 3% range' over the next four years through disciplined budgeting, responsible growth and 'getting London's fair share from Ottawa and Queen's Park'
Would keep securing federal/provincial grants and maintain London's strong credit rating to keep borrowing costs down
Pledges every tax dollar should produce visible value (housing, transit, parks, roads, public safety, libraries) and to lead advocacy for a fairer municipal finance system
positions.verbatim_quote: We will hold property tax increases in the 3% range over the next four years by focusing on disciplined budgeting, responsible growth, smarter use of every tax dollar, and getting London's fair share from Ottawa and Queen's Park.
positions.source_title: Re-Elect Josh Morgan for Mayor (campaign platform)

positions.summary_short: Morgan's downtown plan centres on a cultural-hub vision, a public-private parking facility, and commercial vacancy reduction.
summary_bullets: Would make downtown London's cultural hub with more events, hospitality, public spaces and year-round reasons to visit, partnering with other large cities and Ottawa on a national downtown-revitalization push
Through a public-private partnership, would create a premier parking facility downtown with EV charging and secure bike storage

Would reduce commercial vacancies via community improvement programs, an aggressive economic development strategy and a new strategic-assets development program; cites advancing Phase 5 of Innovation Park for industrial jobs
positions.verbatim_quote: Downtown should be the place people want to live and visit, not avoid.
positions.source_title: Re-Elect Josh Morgan for Mayor (campaign platform)

positions.summary_short: Morgan would renew the Neighbourhood Parks Improvement Fund and close gaps on the Thames Valley Parkway trail.
summary_bullets: Would renew the Neighbourhood Parks Improvement Fund, building on major park improvements delivered over the past four years
Would close gaps and improve access on the Thames Valley Parkway, 'one of London's greatest natural assets'
Also pledges to cut red tape and work with partners to create more childcare spaces across London
positions.verbatim_quote: We will renew the Neighbourhood Parks Improvement Fund.
positions.source_title: Re-Elect Josh Morgan for Mayor (campaign platform)

positions.summary_short: Stevenson runs on 'compassion with accountability': stronger enforcement, measurable results, and a City Hall package of quarterly spending reviews, an auditor general and a fraud hotline.
summary_bullets: Would restore safety and pride in neighbourhoods through 'compassion with accountability': stronger enforcement, cleaner public spaces, and measurable results; residents should 'feel safe in their parks, on transit, in business districts, and in their own communities'
Would bring accountability back to City Hall via responsible spending and transparent decision-making, and improve transportation through reliable transit and safer roads

Announced (Oct 2026) a financial-disclosure package: quarterly spending reviews, an independent auditor general, a fraud and waste hotline, and a review of senior administration costs (reported by CBC)
positions.verbatim_quote: Residents deserve to feel safe in their parks, on transit, in business districts, and in their own communities. London needs compassion with accountability, stronger enforcement, cleaner public spaces, and measurable results.
positions.source_title: Susan Stevenson for Mayor of London (priorities)

positions.summary_short: Stevenson would review homelessness spending, overhaul housing supports, and advocate for a provincial addiction treatment centre with sober, recovery-focused housing.
summary_bullets: Promised a review of homelessness spending, an overhaul of housing supports, and continued advocacy for a provincially funded addiction treatment centre

Advocates sober, recovery-focused housing; in her own statement she says 'Mental health, addiction, and homelessness require stronger partnerships with healthcare providers and other governments' and that 'The city needs to change our policies to focus on recovery and measurable results'
Campaigned on an end to public drug use
positions.verbatim_quote: The city needs to change our policies to focus on recovery and measurable results.
positions.source_title: Susan Stevenson makes her play | Josh Morgan pushes back (City Hall Notes, via London Free Press / CTV London)

positions.summary_short: Stevenson promises a review of rapid-transit spending and road construction.
summary_bullets: Is promising a review of BRT (rapid transit) spending and road construction
Has opposed the trajectory of the current BRT program, which has seen budgets rise and corridors cancelled (north and west legs)
positions.verbatim_quote: Mayoral candidate Susan Stevenson, for example, is promising a review of BRT spending and road construction.
positions.source_title: Election 2026: so many promises (Buckle Up, The Loon)

positions.summary_short: Stevenson supports a renoviction bylaw with enforcement and partnerships to expand housing options.
summary_bullets: Supports a renoviction bylaw with enforcement (per Ontarians Against Corruption's platform tracking)
Says the City should change its policies to focus on recovery and measurable results on homelessness, and supports partnerships that expand housing options

positions.summary_short: Krose would turn housing approvals into completed homes, encourage missing-middle housing, and publish an annual Housing and Homelessness Report Card.
summary_bullets: Would turn housing approvals into homes: continue improving development approvals, publish approval timelines, and identify barriers preventing approved units from reaching construction
Would encourage more kinds of homes (missing-middle, additional residential units, thoughtful intensification where infrastructure allows)
Growth must strengthen the tax base, not create unfunded liabilities: 'Today's development decisions become tomorrow's infrastructure bills'
Would publish an annual Housing and Homelessness Report Card tracking approvals, permits, starts, completions, affordable and supportive housing, and homelessness inflow/outflow
positions.verbatim_quote: London's challenge is no longer simply approving more units. We need to turn approvals into homes while making sure growth creates strong communities rather than tomorrow's infrastructure problems.

positions.summary_short: Krose would launch a London Performance Dashboard in her first 100 days and require every major proposal to answer four accountability questions.
summary_bullets: First-100-days commitments: launch the London Performance Dashboard, begin a rotating program-review cycle, start a citywide service-timeliness and permitting review, and modernize development approvals
Every major proposal coming to City Hall should answer four questions: Is it municipal? What problem does it solve? How will we know if it worked? What is the full cost to taxpayers?
Platform stance: 'The answer is not automatically bigger government or smaller government. It is government that performs better'
positions.verbatim_quote: The answer is not automatically bigger government or smaller government. It is government that performs better.
positions.source_title: Platform | Kirsten Krose for Mayor (First 100 Days)

positions.summary_short: Krose would start a Traffic Bottleneck Program and rank school-zone risks, tying infrastructure planning to housing growth.
summary_bullets: Would establish a Traffic Bottleneck Program and complete the first school-zone risk ranking in her first 100 days
Would plan infrastructure alongside housing so roads, transit, water, wastewater, parks and community services keep pace with growth
positions.verbatim_quote: Today's development decisions become tomorrow's infrastructure bills, so growth should strengthen London's tax base rather than create unfunded liabilities for future taxpayers.
positions.source_title: Platform | Kirsten Krose for Mayor (First 100 Days)

positions.summary_short: Krose favours practical climate resilience, potentially restoring the $1M/year Climate Change Reserve Fund tied to clear outcomes.
summary_bullets: Leans toward practical climate resilience that protects critical infrastructure and lowers long-term costs
Leans toward restoring the $1M-a-year Climate Change Reserve Fund, with funding tied to clear outcomes rather than an arbitrary level
Leans toward tougher 2050 walking, cycling and transit targets if they are realistic, evidence-based and matched by real service and infrastructure improvements
positions.verbatim_quote: Practical climate resilience that protects critical infrastructure and lowers long-term costs.
positions.source_title: Kirsten Krose (Ontarians Against Corruption candidate profile)

positions.summary_short: Morgan would run one honest review of City Hall's systems, rewrite everything in plain language, hold monthly public meetings, and serve a single term.
summary_bullets: Would conduct 'one honest review' of how the City runs — bylaws, policies, contracts, meetings, administration — asking: is it working, can people understand it, is there waste, is it fair
Every bylaw, notice, contract and budget in plain language; transparent, even-handed bylaw enforcement and less over-regulation for small businesses
Shorter council meetings, fewer closed-door sessions, and a public meeting every month somewhere different in the city
Running for one term only, by choice: 'No re-election math, just the honest work of handing the city over in better shape'
positions.verbatim_quote: One honest review of how the City runs, and everything it unlocks.
positions.source_title: The plan · Bronagh Joyce Morgan for Mayor

positions.summary_short: Morgan would cut admin overhead from homelessness contracts, write long-term fair contracts, and publish honest outcome measures.
summary_bullets: Would cut administrative overhead out of the City's homelessness-service contracts to get money to front-line workers
Would write watertight, fair, long-term contracts that treat homelessness as a long-term human crisis, not a line item re-litigated every budget cycle
Would publish honest public measurement so Londoners can see what is working and what isn't
positions.verbatim_quote: Watertight, fair, long-term contracts that treat homelessness as the long-term human crisis it is, not a line item to re-litigate every budget cycle.
positions.source_title: The plan · Bronagh Joyce Morgan for Mayor

summary_bullets: Safer neighbourhoods as a campaign pillar
A street that feels safe after dark as a basic expectation
positions.summary_short: Krose focuses on safer neighbourhoods as part of her basics-first platform.
positions.verbatim_quote: focused on reliable services, shorter commutes, safer neighbourhoods, and respect for every tax dollar.

summary_bullets: A budget that respects taxpayers' paycheques
The basics are the whole job - not too much to ask
positions.summary_short: Krose promises a budget that respects taxpayers' paycheques.
positions.verbatim_quote: a bus that comes on time, a street that feels safe after dark, and a budget that respects your paycheque are too much to ask. I don't believe that.

positions.source_title: Meet Kirsten | Kirsten Krose for Mayor
summary_bullets: Support local kids and families via community organizations like BGC
Champion housing-with-dignity efforts like Homes for Heroes
positions.summary_short: Krose highlights community work with BGC, neighbourhood groups and Homes for Heroes.
positions.verbatim_quote: Supporting local kids and families through community organizations like BGC - because every young Londoner deserves a place to belong and grow.
